reconcile.connective: Defenders read the two notices as complementary: Ahaz was buried in the city of David, but pointedly excluded from the royal sepulchres as a mark of disgrace.

discrepancy.connective: Steve Wells, cataloguing the passage in the Skeptic's Annotated Bible, presses the plain wording: 2 Chronicles 28:27 contradicts 2 Kings 16:20 over where Ahaz was laid — buried 'with his fathers' versus kept out of the kings' tombs.

excerpts.excerpt_text: Was buried with his fathers in the city of David — But it is expressly declared, Ch2 28:27, that he was not buried in the sepulchres of the kings of Israel; and this was undoubtedly intended as a mark of degradation.
excerpts.on_tension_rationale: Clarke reads both verses together — 2 Kings 16:20 'buried with his fathers in the city of David' and 2 Chronicles 28:27 'not buried in the sepulchres of the kings' — and harmonizes the difference as a deliberate posthumous mark of degradation rather than a conflict. The single strongest reconcile naming both passages.

pd_work.note: Clarke treats this exact pair, reconciling 2 Kings 16:20 with the 2 Chronicles 28:27 qualifier as one consistent burial-in-Jerusalem-minus-royal-tombs notice. Used in place of Haley, whose specific coverage of this passage could not be confirmed.
